text:
eli: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a compact rollout/epoch metadata that clients can resolve cheaply. idea: single source of truth for "epoch" + stable aliases + retire windows so clients can decide fallbacks without a big lookup.
sara: can you sketch the minimal fields? worried about adding another surface for client compatibility.
eli: sure. minimal proposal:
```
{
  "epoch": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z",   // opaque version token for rollouts
  "aliases": ["stable", "canary-42"],
  "cohorts": ["beta", "global"],
  "soft_retire_ts": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
  "hard_retire_ts": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "fallback_order": ["stable","fallback-legacy"],
  "compat_hashes": ["sha256:abcd..."]
}
```
jon: I like epoch as an opaque token. question: should clients treat soft_retire as a hint or an enforced error if they request by alias?
eli: intent is hint. client can warn or start shifting cohorts. enforced errors only at hard_retire.
kevin: we need to be explicit about semantics for aliases vs canonical epoch. e.g., alias -> epoch binding must be monotonic within a tenant to avoid flapping.
sara: monotonic binding + generation number would help. maybe add "gen": 7 to the object so clients can detect rebinds.
eli: good call. add `gen` and maybe `source` for provenance (control-plane, infra, manual).
jon: telemetry: we should emit events when clients resolve alias->epoch and when they fall back. helps debug regens.
devops-bot: deploy-log: rollout-metadata-service v2 deployed to staging at 4287654400
kevin: minor nit: compatibility hashes list could blow up. recommend optional and truncated fingerprints for quick checks.
eli: agree optional. also recommend TTL on alias cache for clients — default 30s but configurable per-tenant.
sara: one more: how do we handle multi-model rollouts (ensemble)? do we let epoch point to a list of model refs?
eli: epoch can be lightweight pointer. we can add `models: ["m:resnet-v2","m:text-3b@sha..."]` but keep it optional — core clients only need epoch + fallback.
jon: action items: 1) elicit team to add `gen` and `source` to the draft. 2) ops to add telemetry hooks for resolve/fallback. 3) write client cache guidance (TTL + backoff).
kevin: I'll take #2. will add metrics: alias_resolve_latency, alias_rebind_count, alias_fallback_rate.
sara: I'll draft the client guidance doc. include examples for pin-by-epoch and pin-by-alias.
eli: thanks — once we have docs + telemetry we'll run a small canary on Dedicated for two tenants.
jon: LGTM overall. keep the schema intentionally minimal to avoid coupling.
kevin: +1
eli: thanks everyone. follow-up mtg if needed — ping me.
